$comment: Machine-readable description of the reference corpus. Read by hand today, by
LexiSharp.Cli once the verify mode lands. Nothing here is a pass/fail gate yet:
the expectations are hypotheses to be checked, not facts.
name: LexiSharp reference corpus
buildPath: one-shot Index() over the whole directory; never incremental Add/Remove
$harnessCaveat: The 'expects' blocks below describe how the STOCK configurations shipped with
LexiSharp.Cli should separate these cases: bm25, bm25-semantic (PMI term
The dense capability in this repository is HashingEmbeddingProvider, which is
NOT a semantic model: it is feature hashing over the tokens, so it captures
lexical overlap and nothing else. Any expectation phrased as 'dense misses'
here is therefore a statement about hashing, and is a LOWER BOUND proxy for a
real embedding model, not a stand-in for one. A real dense model may well
separate the identifier and synonym cases. Do not read these as claims about

identifier.intent: A query that is an opaque literal. Lexical matching should win decisively; nothing in the vocabulary overlaps.

expects.bm25: finds the exact document at rank 1
expects.dense: no principled reason to separate MZ-77E2T0 from MZ-77E2T1 or MZ-77E2T9 - all three share a shape

synonym.intent: Query and document share no vocabulary. Only a synonym edge or a corpus-derived association can close the gap.

expects.bm25-semantic: can succeed via PmiTermExpander, provided the corpus actually associates automobile with car

paraphrase.intent: The user asks about a symptom ('recover a lost password'), the document is written about the mechanism ('credential rotation').

expects.bm25-semantic: partial, and only if the corpus co-occurs the two vocabularies

rare-term.intent: A term appearing in a single document. Its IDF is maximal, so a single match should outweigh a term common across the corpus.

expects.bm25: the rare term alone should carry the match
expects.note: this family is also a guard on the opposite failure: a document stuffed with common words outranking a precise rare-term hit

multilingual.intent: The same fact in English, French and German. The stock tokenizer folds diacritics and lowercases but does NOT translate or stem across languages.

expects.bm25: matches same-language text; cross-language recall depends entirely on a stemmer or a translation step being supplied

long-document.intent: The answer sits in a document several hundred words long, next to two near neighbours that differ by one word.

expects.bm25: length normalization should keep the long document competitive; without it, TF dilution buries it
expects.note: a long document is also the adversarial input for a term expander: PMI associations learned from it are mostly noise

ambiguous.intent: One symptom, several documents, only one of which is the actual cause. THIS is the family the graded qrels exist for.

expects.bm25: the diagnosis should outrank the workaround
expects.note: a binary qrels file would score all three documents equally and could not express the distinction this family exists to test

metadata-conflict.intent: The document body and its front-matter fields disagree about what it is about.

expects.bm25: ranks on body text; a metadata filter is a separate, explicit gate and is not part of the ranking

ordinary.intent: Plain, well-matched documents. They exist so that IDF and average document length are not degenerate, and so that the hard families are not the only signal in the corpus.

expects.bm25: should be near-perfect; a failure here means the tokenizer, the index or the scorer is broken, not tuned

$note: The ratio is a starting point, not a result. A corpus of only hard cases makes
IDF and average document length meaningless; a corpus of only ordinary cases
has nothing to discriminate. Target for the full corpus is roughly 70% ordinary
by count, reviewed after the first verify run against the measured spread.
